title: Visit of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyz Republic (29 August-1 September 2026)
body_text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit Uzbekistan from 29–30 August on a bilateral visit and the Kyrgyz Republic for the 26th SCO Summit from 31 August to 1 September 2026. At the invitation of the President of Uzbekistan, H.E. Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev, Prime Minister will undertake a State Visit to Tashkent on 29–30 August 2026. This will be Prime Minister’s fourth visit to Uzbekistan. During the visit, Prime Minister will hold delegation-level talks with President Mirziyoyev to further strengthen the strategic partnership between the two countries. The two leaders would review cooperation in trade and investment, defence, digital connectivity, energy, education and people-to-people domains and set the agenda for the road ahead. They will also share perspectives on advancing the shared developmental visions of Viksit Bharat 2047 and Uzbekistan-2030. Prime Minister is also expected to visit the Shastri Memorial in Tashkent and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies. From Tashkent, at the invitation of the President of Kyrgyz Republic, H.E. Mr. Sadyr Zhaparov, Prime Minister will travel to Bishkek to participate in the 26th SCO Summit on 31 August – 1 September 2026. The Summit marks the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, of which India has been a full member since 2017. Prime Minister will address the Summit where he will highlight India’s priorities of Security, Connectivity and Opportunity at the forum. Prime Minister will also hold bilateral meetings with SCO leaders on the sidelines of the Summit. He will also attend the Opening Ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games, a celebration of the rich cultural heritage of Central Asia.

enrichment.summary: PM Narendra Modi will undertake a State Visit to Uzbekistan on 29-30 August 2026, followed by participation in the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic, from 31 August to 1 September 2026. In Tashkent he will hold talks with President Mirziyoyev covering trade, defence, connectivity, energy and education, and visit the Shastri Memorial and Mahatma Gandhi Centre. At the SCO Summit, marking the organisation's 25th anniversary, Modi will highlight India's priorities of Security, Connectivity and Opportunity and hold bilateral meetings with SCO leaders, and will also attend the opening of the 6th World Nomad Games.
enrichment.context: India has been deepening ties with Central Asian states as part of its 'Connect Central Asia' policy, with Uzbekistan being a key partner in energy, connectivity and counter-terrorism cooperation. India became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in 2017, and the SCO Summit serves as a platform for India to engage with China, Russia, Pakistan and Central Asian states on regional security, connectivity (including alternatives to China's Belt and Road Initiative), and economic cooperation. This release is a pre-visit itinerary announcement without substantive policy outcomes, agreements, or joint statements, making it primarily informational rather than a landmark development in itself.
